points.description: Defines an artificial neural network as a network/processor made of many simple processing units (neurons) working in parallel/distributed fashion that stores knowledge from experience and makes it available for use.
points.partial_credit: Half if vague, e.g. just 'a system of connected units/neurons' with no mention of simple units, parallel processing or storing knowledge.

points.description: States how it resembles the brain: knowledge is acquired from the environment through learning, and connection strengths between neurons (synaptic weights) store the knowledge.
points.partial_credit: Half if only one of the two resemblances is given, or if the resemblance is stated only vaguely (e.g. 'it has neurons like the brain').

rubric.notes: Full marks: a recognisable definition (simple connected units processing in parallel, storing knowledge from experience) plus the brain resemblance (learning from environment; weights/connection strengths store knowledge), in any wording. Part marks: vague or incomplete definition, or only one of the two resemblances. Zero: off-topic or wrong answers; extra incorrect remarks do not cost marks unless they contradict the core idea.
